summary: Assembly's WRITE-provider guard only rejects known legacy classes and labels; it never positively requires a ContainedWriteWorkspaceProvider or ContainedGateRunner for workspace.contained / gates.contained descriptors.
failure_scenario: A WRITE-capable ExecutorProvider plus an arbitrary host-executing object catalogued as kind 'workspace.contained' (or 'gates.contained' that is neither GateRunner nor BoundGateRunner) is accepted by Constructicon(); the comment 'check the actual resources too' implies a physical check, but only negative class membership is tested. Containment then relies solely on the codex executor's later isinstance re-check (codex.py ~1696/1827), so any other WRITE provider gets no such protection.
evidence: Ran a temporary pytest (deleted afterwards): FakeExecutorProvider with WRITE posture + plain class instance with CapabilityDescriptor(kind='workspace.contained', requires_posture=WRITE) -> Constructicon(...) constructed with no error. Only ContainedGateRunner instances get a descriptor-vs-resource check (system.py:195-200); no such check exists for the contained workspace.

summary: The relabel test uses only the real legacy classes, so it passes through the isinstance(GitWorkspaceCapability/GateRunner) clause and never exercises an arbitrary relabeled lookalike resource.
failure_scenario: Removing the requirement that a workspace.contained descriptor be backed by a contained provider (or adding a lookalike) leaves every case green; the acceptance path for a non-contained object labelled contained is untested and in fact currently accepted.
evidence: Read the test; parametrization is legacy in {workspace,gates} x relabel x posture using object.__new__ of the legacy classes. The probe above shows a plain object is accepted.

summary: test_entry_refuses_mismatched_authority_before_startup asserts a bare ContractViolation for seven different mutations, which all share one error message in the single conjunction in require_maintenance_attempt.
failure_scenario: If one clause of the conjunction (e.g. workspace pin or journal path) were deleted, another mutated field or an unrelated ContractViolation (such as the earlier require_maintenance_resources check) would still raise and the test would stay green; no case covers attempt_record/journal path-shape clauses or descriptor/executor_incoherence at all.
evidence: Read src maintenance_entry.py require_maintenance_attempt (one boolean over ~20 clauses, one message) and the test. Not mutation-tested. Focused suite passes (90 passed).

summary: OAuth actor tests cover only one token; they never show that different issuer/subject/client_id produce different actor ids, that a missing iss/sub degrades predictably, or that ADMIN scope passes through, and no MCP test exercises a scope refusal or the HTTP/OAuth server path.
failure_scenario: A regression dropping 'issuer' or 'client_id' from the principal digest, or letting a stdio-only scope path through, would not fail any test in this slice (tests/api/mcp/test_server.py only uses StaticActorSource with success paths).
evidence: Read test_auth.py, test_server.py, test_capability_accounting.py; all MCP calls use StaticActorSource and succeed.

summary: mcp/server.py lifespan: MCPServer enters the lifespan once per streamable-HTTP manager run (streamable_http_manager.py:142), so ControlPlane.shutdown (permanent) is not triggered per stateless request.

mcp/auth.py: actor id is a domain-separated digest of (issuer, subject, client_id) matching mcp principal_components; scopes are intersected with CONTROL_SCOPES; static actors cannot be built from tool args.
mcp/__main__.py: streamable-http refuses to start without verifier, issuer and resource URL; stdio scopes only come from the launcher.

plan_manifest_application.derive_maintenance_result: single-parent candidate, raw diff-tree single 'A' of the vector path, tested_tree/merge-commit parents, attestation run/manifest/check-set binding are all verified; fixed check pins every base blob by oid and mode. Post-run executor grants/capability_id are derived from the manifest itself, but pre-run require_maintenance_attempt and acquisition-time authorization pin them, so no exploit found.

Focused tests for mcp, maintenance_entry and plan_manifest_application: 90 passed.
